clue.text: Review in a paper is flawed

indicators.note: something flawed is faulty, so the words a paper is are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a review appearing in some newspaper is badly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the IS belongs to the fodder, leaving 'flawed' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to assess its worth, which is what a review does.

clue.text: A second source found, too

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone tracking a story has turned up another informant as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean additionally, in addition.

clue.text: Peak rates for birds

indicators.note: read as 'making', the letters of peak rates are turned into another word for the birds

explanation.surface: A complaint about the highest prices charged for pet birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is very slight: 'for' has to be read as 'to make', so PEAK RATES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small long-tailed parrots, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Some of them will come from Basra

definitions.text: Some of them will come from Basra

indicators.note: the letters of the word Basra are the source from which a new word is made by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark that a share of a group of people hail from the Iraqi city of Basra.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: rearrange BASRA, and Basra is an Iraqi city whose people are largely Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is a city in Iraq, an Arab country, so its people are mostly of that ethnic group.

clue.text: Summoned for misappropriation of rents

indicators.note: misappropriation means wrongful use, here the letters of of rents are put to a different use

explanation.surface: A landlord's agent was called in over rent money going astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; the fodder is OF RENTS, not RENTS alone.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone has been called to come, they have been summoned.

clue.text: Stays with a sailor on a date in Rome

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
the Ides was a fixed date in the ancient Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: Someone spends time with a seaman during a romantic date in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or stay in a place.

clue.text: Continued to argue terms-lawyers benefited

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to have gained is to have benefited

explanation.surface: Negotiations dragged on over conditions, and the attorneys were the ones who profited.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to keep disputing the conditions of a deal.

clue.text: Don't struggle to get the meaning

explanation.definitionFit: To go with the flow without resisting, as a boat does on a current; also the gist or general sense of what someone says.

clue.text: Large town supports a legend of wisdom

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a saga is a long legendary tale
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A big town is the backing for a famous tale of sagacious people.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness and sound judgement are what this word names, a synonym of good sense.

clue.text: Means to put on a brave face

definitions.text: Means to put on a brave face

parts.words: Means to put on a brave face
parts.note: literally a substance a fighter applies to the face to look fierce before battle, disguised as the idiom for hiding fear

explanation.surface: A phrase about keeping up a show of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors painted their faces with it before going into battle, so it is literally a way of putting on a bold face.

clue.text: Airing some laundry in good weather

indicators.note: some of means only part of the run of words laundry in good is used

explanation.surface: A remark about putting washing out when the weather is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weather' finishes the picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing clothes is drying them out by exposure.

clue.text: Shoot game

explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph, as in to take a photo; also a children's card game where matching cards are called out.

clue.text: Amounts of water coming from leaks

indicators.note: a new word coming from leaks is built out of that word's rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Puddles forming from leaking pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakes are bodies of water.

clue.text: Worker in firm put in charge? Great!

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: fast means firm, as in holding fast
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee at a company gets promoted to the top job, and everyone cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are enthusiastic exclamations of approval, meaning wonderful.

clue.text: N. African halves a number then doubles it

indicators.note: doubles it means the kept piece is written out twice
halves here means only the second half of the word number is kept

explanation.surface: A North African performs some arithmetic: halving a figure and then doubling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halves' keeps BER from NUMBER; 'doubles it' writes that twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are an indigenous people of North Africa.

clue.text: Bring round advance payment? Just joking!

indicators.note: round means bring wraps around the other piece

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in advance in poker

explanation.surface: Someone asked to bring a deposit replies that they were only kidding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring round' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'round' is the container signal: the word bring wraps the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing talk is playful joking, so the word fits a declaration of not being serious.

clue.text: Sharp bet using inside information

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a punt is a bet in British slang
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A shrewd wager made with insider tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or remark is sharp and biting.

clue.text: Leader of a column?

parts.note: reads like the person at the head of a marching line, but means a newspaper's leading article, which fills a column

explanation.surface: Who heads a military column?
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leader is its opinion piece, so this is a column-length leading article.

clue.text: Jumper having a pocket in front

definitions.text: Jumper having a pocket in front

parts.words: Jumper having a pocket in front
parts.note: sounds like a knitted top with a front pocket, but means a leaping marsupial carrying a pouch

explanation.surface: A sweater with a pouch pocket on the front.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian animal hops and carries its young in a pouch on its belly.

clue.text: Footballers' magazine

explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club; also a store of weapons and ammunition, which is one sense of magazine.

clue.text: Dead slow

explanation.definitionFit: Late means deceased, as in the late king; also behind time, tardy.

clue.text: Consecrate a Rodin sculpture

indicators.note: sculpture suggests shaping material, so the letters of a Rodin are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A church blesses a work by the French sculptor Rodin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to make holy or to admit formally to the priesthood.

clue.text: One who is against work has a problem

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A dissenter dislikes a job that is causing difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone who argues against.

clue.text: Strays around in the woods

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of strays are moved about

explanation.surface: Wanderers roaming through a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: these creatures of myth roam the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are goat-like woodland spirits of Greek myth, roaming forests.

clue.text: See post go out in March

indicators.note: out signals the letters of see post go are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone watches a fence post being removed in the third month.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff-legged military step is a way of marching.

clue.text: Girl getting a first love letter

indicators.note: first puts this piece at the head of the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl receives her first love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Incorrect teaspoon set out in Indian city

indicators.note: incorrect signals the letters are mixed up; the letters of set are taken out of teaspoon

explanation.surface: Someone sets the wrong spoon on the table in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' means the letters S, E, T come out of TEASPOON, leaving APOON to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona, now Pune, is a city in Maharashtra, India.

clue.text: Tidy up? No, down!

parts.note: a bird tidies its soft feathers, its down, rather than tidying up a room

explanation.surface: A correction: not straightening up, but straightening down.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds smooth and clean their feathers with the beak, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Rush upon it and revise once more

parts.note: a reed is a rush, a marsh plant

explanation.surface: Hurry onto the task and go over it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb meaning hurry; it is the marsh plant, and 'upon' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit again is to correct a text a second time.

clue.text: In a way it repays harshness

indicators.note: in a way suggests the words it repays are taken in some other form

explanation.surface: Being severe can pay off in some respects.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or severity of manner.

clue.text: Coloured ring on compass

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
compass means range or scope

explanation.surface: A painted circle drawn with a pair of compasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour, so as an adjective it means having a certain hue.

clue.text: Crumbs are slung out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of are slung are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Bits of food get thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Granules are small grains or particles.
